newsitem.title: UK: Net flows to Europe mutual funds slow in Aug - poll.
newsitem.headline: Net flows to Europe mutual funds slow in Aug - poll.

text.p: Investors' interest in European mutual funds slowed in August, the lull coinciding with the traditional holiday season, the latest monthly survey on fund flows from J.P. Morgan showed.
Italy and Spain saw net redemptions from their domestic equity funds but continued to enjoy strong flows into their fixed income funds, according to the research conducted by analyst Caroline Meroz.

Sweden and the Netherlands, in contrast, saw active buying of both international and domestic equities. Swedish mutual funds have maintained a substantial 70-80 percent in equities, but Dutch mutual funds have been pushing up equity holdings to around 40 percent from just 30 percent two years ago.

Meroz said the most noticeable improvement in fund flows in August was in France, where domestic equity SICAVs (Societes d'Investissment a Capital Variable) broke even for the first time since July 1995.

"In addtion, net redmeptions from bond funds slowed sharply, possibly indicating an improvement in investor confidence," she said. "We believe that recent changes to the taxation of life insurance policies will have a limited but positive impact on mutual fund inflows."
She added that data for September should begin to reflect the markets' positive reactions to the budget season and renewed hopes of early-stage EMU participation for Italy and Spain.
In the U.S., the survey showed mutual funds recovered from lows in July and attracted $15 billion net new investment into domestic equities in August.
"This improvement was also reflected in higher net subscriptions to international-only funds, which took in $2.3 billion, bringing the total net inflow for the year to $23 billion," Meroz said.
